newsitem.title: USA: Senate Republican leaders talk before Clinton meet.
newsitem.headline: Senate Republican leaders talk before Clinton meet.

text.p: Senate Republican leaders met Tuesday morning in advance of their afternoon meeting with President Clinton but said little about their 1997 agenda.
"We're interested in hearing what (Clinton) has to say," Majority Leader Trent Lott of Mississippi told reporters.
He said Republicans would wait until Clinton submitted his budget next year before making any decisions on budget issues.
"I don't think you're going to see anything substantive out of this meeting," Lott said of the meeting with Clinton, House Republican leaders and Democratic congressional leaders.

"We look forward to working for the people's agenda," Lott said. On Saturday, he said Republicans would cooperate with Clinton if Clinton was sincere about balancing the budget and reducing the size of government.

Lott also said he had not counted votes among newly elected senators for a constitutional amendment to require a balanced budget. The amendment passed the House in 1995 but failed in the Senate by one vote. Republicans will have a 55-45 Senate majority in the next Congress, two seats more than their current margin.
